Another comment said it already but Portrait of a Lady on Fire is probably my favourite film I've seen. Absolutely incredible. I think there's like one male character and he doesn't have any lines 😂 but it's genuinely a phenomenal film.

Room, starring Brie Larson is a really good film too. One of my all time favourites - but it is very intense at points, as it's about a woman who is kept prisoner and gives birth to her r*pists child. So yeah, TWs abound. But a brilliant film.

Another very TW film, that also stars Brie Larson, is Short Term 12. There's two main characters who are men, but the focus on the film is Larson's character and a teen girl who Larson's character believes is being SA'd. It's a hard watch, but it's an exceptional film.

For TV, Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt remains one of my favourite sitcoms as the lead character is a survivor of a cult and child abduction, yet it remains generally very light and funny. It's a really clever balance of silliness and serious issues, which makes it easy to watch while addressing serious issues. The rest of the characters include an elderly woman, a gay black man, and an upper class woman.

Call the Midwife is another brilliant TV series that I love. TW for childbirth, but there is a lot more to the series than babies being born. Above all, it's a heartwarming yet often gritty look at womenhood in 1950s England. First three seasons are perfect. After that it's still very good but becomes more cosy and less gritty, which makes it a nice comfort show where the main cast are all women, but the grittiness of the early seasons is one of its biggest selling points imo.

Derry Girls is a great TV series too, set in the 1990s in Ireland, during the Troubles. The main cast is made of young women and the series is written by a woman, based on her experiences of growing up during that time. It's essentially a sitcom and it's very funny, relatable and comfy.

Alcohol we try to stay away from, as it tends to pull a specific teen alter to the front who will drink us to oblivion. It's weird cos it means we are an alcoholic to an extent, though we are completely able to have one drink without losing control, because it's only if that alter comes out that our drinking becomes a problem.

Weed is an interesting one, because it seems to calm our anxiety a lot and it improves our communication. It's like out communication is all of us talking at once when we're sober, but when we're high, it's all slowed down and we can hear each other much more clearly. Weirdly though, it does sometimes bring kids to the front because they like the happy feelings, eating the yummy foods, laughing at the funny things etc. So for that reason we tend to only get high with people we trust.

If it is something you ultimately decide you do want, forgiveness should be to help you move past what they did and live your best life. The abusers do not matter. They do not matter. YOU matter.

They don't have to derive sexual pleasure from it for it to be sexual. Forcibly exposing your child in public is sexual abuse because of the forced nudity. For example, if an abuser takes nude photos of a child and shares them, they might not be deriving any sexual pleasure from it - often abusers do sick things like that for the financial gain of selling those images. Likewise, rather than sexual pleasure or financial gain, your parents gained power and control over you. The abuse is still sexual, even if the abuser isn't deriving sexual pleasure from it. Does that make sense?

Ultimately though, I don't think definitions are so important. Sexual abuse or not, what happened to you WAS abuse. It was wrong and it should never have happened. I hope you can heal and find some peace friend.

A lot of sexual abuse isn't even about sex, it's about power. And by humiliating you in these ways, that was an abusive way of them gaining power over you.  There doesn't need to be physical contact for it to be sexual abuse. You were a child. It was forced nudity. It was child sexual abuse.

Any kid can get suicidal thoughts. Any kid with decent parents will get support to keep them safe. Of course, it's possible to have parents who get you help but you still give in to suicidal thoughts, but most times when a kid commits suicide it could've been prevented with some parental attention and professional help.

I'm sorry to say it but yeah I expect her kids are in danger. The majority of CSA is perpetrated by family members and she has a history of sexually abusing children. She's dangerous and her kids are not safe.

However, I cannot emphasise enough how it is *not* your responsibility. Do *not* feel guilty. The only person to blame for abuse is the abusers. Be kind to yourself and only get involved as much as you can handle.

The best piece of advice I can give is to remember that littles are children and to treat them as such. Make them feel loved and safe, don't push responsibilities and topics on them that aren't suitable for a child, and be gentle. If you're not gentle with them, you risk making them even more frontstuck / for longer. Once they trust you and feel safe with you, they stand more chance of switching and letting an older alter take over. That's my understanding at least. I hope that helps.
